record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a truncated file listing only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes applying a rank-1 runtime refusal-direction ablation and says the resulting model answers questions stock DeepSeek refuses. This is a qualitative test of removal, not the original difference-in-means measurement and intervention in a controlled study.
record.gate_note: The README attributes refusal-rate and HumanEval results (98.3% to 4.2%; 95.1% to 95.7%) to the adapter author’s measurements on Maya, so they are cited results and are not recorded as this repository’s results. The repository’s own speed comparisons do not measure refusal or general capability.
record.test_reason: The repository is an inference rig. It applies a third-party rank-1 refusal-direction adapter at runtime as a tool. Its own measurements are speed, VRAM and vision checks, and none measures refusal. The only refusal statement is an unquantified line that the model answers questions stock DeepSeek refuses. It gives no prompts, count, rate or control. The refusal and HumanEval numbers (98.3%→4.2%, 95.1%→95.7%) are the adapter author's measurements on Maya, cited rather than produced here. So the repository relies on the finding and reports only its own engineering performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The README presents a Windows rig that runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at about 38 tok/s with vision. A reversible rank-1 abliteration adapter is projected out at runtime, with zero speed cost on the rig. The README asserts, without measurement, that the model answers questions stock DeepSeek refuses. Refusal and capability numbers are deferred to the adapter author's Maya measurements.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a rank-1 adapter and runtime projection across attention and MoE writes; the README does not say this direction was derived by the original difference-in-means procedure. This is a Windows rig/tool built on upstream Strata, which the README links as its base.
record.problems: The repository’s own refusal evidence is qualitative and lacks a prompt count, refusal rate, or stated control procedure. The numerical refusal and HumanEval results are attributed to the adapter author’s Maya measurements, not to this repository’s own test.
record.rows_left_out: No repository results on refusal or capability beyond the qualitative statement in R1. The README’s adapter-author Maya metrics are cited results and excluded; speed benchmarks do not measure claim outcomes.

untested.parts: Refusal rate under ablation, adding the direction to induce refusal, how the direction was derived, and capability retention (the HumanEval numbers are cited from the adapter author).
No weight-edited model is evaluated; the ablation is applied as runtime projection, and no refusal outcome is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Downgraded from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The reader's limits_scope label on V1 was removed because no refusal result is measured by this repository. The 'zero speed' A/B with the adapter on or off is a throughput measure, not a capability or refusal measure. The code (the --ablate port of project-maya PR #469) and the linked docs were not read.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state how the adapter direction was derived or test adding it, measure refusal rates, establish that refusal is removed generally, or report an assessment of other abilities.
The README describes runtime projection with an adapter, not a weight edit, and reports no refusal outcome from a released weight-edited model.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No harmfulness judgment versus refusal-decision separation is tested.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
